summary: Sparse tagged-field block of the sequence (SEQ) reader: a 32-bit presence bitmask followed by the present 32-bit values packed in bit order, read one tag at a time by 0x00661534; the Sound_SeqField_Get* accessors wrap that lookup with a fallback default.
evidence: 0x00661534(base,out,tag) does mask=[base], counts the set bits 0..tag and returns [base+count*4] (disassembly at 0x00661534: tst r6,r7,lsl ip loop, then ldr r0,[r0,r3,lsl #2]). Every Sound_SeqField_Get* calls it with a fixed tag and a fallback (0x40/0x60/0x7F/1/-1). The callers pass DIFFERENT sub-records: Sound_Seq_GetVoiceSlot (0x006604F8) passes the row from func_0065E9D4, Sound_Seq_GetVoiceParamsBase (0x00660C30) passes func_0065F678(self->f_3c), Sound_Seq_GetTrackKindBase (0x006612B4) passes func_0066002C(...). So +0xC/+0x14/+0x18 are block positions inside those records and cannot all live in one 64-byte object; only +0x3C is a field of the outer sequence-data object. Treat this class as a grouping of accessors over the block layout, not as one allocation.

fields.name: maybe_trackKindFieldBlock
fields.evidence: Tag 1 of the block at +0xC is read by Sound_SeqField_GetByte_Off0C (0x0065FD44, default 0x40) and Sound_SeqField_GetFlag_Off0C (0x0065FD6C); Sound_Seq_GetTrackKindBase (0x006612B4) stores both into its track-kind descriptor (out+6 and out+0x19).

fields.name: maybe_voiceParamFieldBlock
fields.evidence: Tags 1, 2, 0x11 and 0x1F of the block at +0x14 are read by GetByte_Off14 (0x0065FED0), GetByteHi_Off14 (0x0065FEF4), GetByte_Off14B (0x0065FFF8), GetByteHi_Off14B (0x0065FFC0), GetFlagBit0_Off14 (0x0065FF74) and GetInt_Off14 (0x0065FF50, default -1); Sound_Seq_GetVoiceParamsBase (0x00660C30) fills the voice parameter block from them.

fields.name: maybe_trackFieldBlock
fields.evidence: Tags 0 and 2 of the block at +0x18 are read by Sound_SeqField_GetByte18 (0x0065FDE0, default 1), GetWord18 (0x0065FDA0) and GetByte18B (0x0065FE24); Sound_SeqTrack_ReadDescriptorA (0x00660E20) uses GetByte18 for the per-track descriptor byte at out+0x3F.

fields.name: seqData
fields.evidence: *(u32*)(self+0x3C) is passed to the record resolver 0x0065F678 (which reads [blob+4] as a table offset and indexes 8-byte entries) and to the self-relative section getters 0x0065FB98 (blob+blob->f_34), 0x0065FBB0 (blob+blob->f_2C) and 0x0065FBC8 (blob+blob->f_1C). Sound_Seq_GetTrackKindBase (0x006612B4) and Sound_Seq_GetVoiceParamsBase (0x00660C30) read the same field as seqData->f_3c.

summary: Resolved wave (sample) handle: points at the wave-archive blob and at one wave record, caches a data offset and a loaded flag, and the Sound_WaveInfo_Copy*/Read* methods unpack the record into the engine's wave descriptor.
evidence: Sound_WaveInfo_CopyDescriptor (0x00660780) copies 0x4C bytes from FUN_0065f324(self->f_4) and branches on the archive version *(u32*)(self->f_0+8) against DAT_00660864; Sound_WaveInfo_CopyHeaderFixed (0x00661480) memcpy's 0x4C bytes from the same source; maybe_Sound_WaveInfo_ParseFormat (0x0065EF6C) reads channel count/format/sample count/loop points from self->f_4 and returns 0 when the byte at +0xC is set. The same 16-byte layout is used by Sound_Resource_CheckMagic (0x006609FC), which reads only +0 and +0xC.

fields.name: archiveBlob
fields.evidence: *(u32*)(self->f_0 + 8) is the wave-archive version compared against DAT_00660864 (CopyDescriptor) and DAT_0065f08c (ParseFormat); FUN_0065f420(self->f_0) returns the archive's data-section offset in maybe_Sound_WaveInfo_GetChannelDataOffset (0x00660A38).

fields.name: waveRecord
fields.evidence: maybe_Sound_WaveInfo_ParseFormat reads channel count at +0, format flag at +1, sample count at +4, loop start/end at +8/+0xC and the channel count again at +0x14 from self->f_4; Sound_WaveInfo_CopySubBlock (0x00660868) indexes its channel table through FUN_0065f308/FUN_0065f358 and bounds-checks against *piVar1.

fields.name: maybe_dataOffset
fields.evidence: maybe_Sound_WaveInfo_ParseFormat passes self->f_2 to FUN_00663380(channelRecord, key), which is `ldr r0,[r0,#4]; add r0,r0,r1` i.e. channelRecord->f_4 + key, and stores the result as the per-channel data pointer at out+0x18+i*0x30.

fields.name: isLoaded
fields.evidence: maybe_Sound_WaveInfo_ParseFormat returns 0 when (char)self->f_3 is nonzero; maybe_Sound_WaveInfo_GetChannelDataOffset (0x00660A38) returns 0 when it is zero; Sound_Resource_CheckMagic (0x006609FC) uses the same byte as the 'resolved' guard before checking the blob magic.

summary: Two-word fade window plus the sound player it belongs to: maybe_Sound_FadeTimer_Get copies one of two word pairs out of the global fade table at 0x0072BD64, choosing the pair by whether the player has a fade pending.
evidence: maybe_Sound_FadeTimer_Get (0x001EF818) writes out[0]/out[1] from 0x0072BD64+0x18/+0x1C when out[2]==0, and from 0x0072BD64+0x10/+0x14 after testing *(u8*)(out[2]+0x194) and calling Sound_GetPlayer (0x006F229C) / 0x001EE018. The readable doc (R3_002) rates this 0.40 and notes there is no caller, so the meaning of the two words is not confirmed.

fields.name: maybe_fadeWindowStart
fields.evidence: *param_1 = uVar2 where uVar2 is 0x0072BD64->f_18 (no fade pending) or 0x0072BD64->f_10 (fade pending); the two words are always copied as a pair, so they are either a 64-bit value or two related scalars - not determined.

fields.name: maybe_fadeWindowEnd
fields.evidence: param_1[1] = uVar5 where uVar5 is 0x0072BD64->f_1c or 0x0072BD64->f_14, the second word of the same pair as offset 0.

fields.name: maybe_soundPlayer
fields.evidence: param_1[2] is null-checked and then *(u8*)(param_1[2]+0x194) is tested as the 'fade pending' flag; when it is set the body calls Sound_GetPlayer (0x006F229C) and 0x001EE018 before reading the other word pair.

summary: A 2D field object that plays a scene BGM when the player taps it: after a 1 s arming delay it waits for the touch event to reach phase 5 and then resolves and commits the scene BGM id.
evidence: Same 972-byte size as Field_Object2D, and the update calls Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState (0x0040D9FC) on the embedded touch event at +0x3B8, which Field_Object2D_BeginTouchEvent (0x0060ED9C) fills and whose timer/state it resets to 0. maybe_Sound_SceneBgmTrigger_Update (0x0060EAE4) adds dt to +0x3C8, flips +0x3C4 from 0 to 1 at 0x3F7FFFFF (~1.0 s), and at 0x3ECCCCCD (0.4 s) with touch phase 5 calls Snd_ResolveSceneBgmId (0x0064C740) and Snd_CommitPendingBgmId (0x001F3AC4/0x001F3820).

fields.name: touchPhase
fields.evidence: FUN_0064C740 is `ldrb r0,[r0]; cmp r0,#5; moveq r0,#1` - it tests the phase byte at +0x3B8 for value 5; Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState (0x0040D9FC) writes the phase into ev[0] and Field_Object2D_BeginTouchEvent stores the 3-byte + 2-word event record at +0x3B8..+0x3C0.

fields.name: state
fields.evidence: 0 = arming delay, 1 = armed: `if (*(char*)(param_1+0x3c4) == 0) { ... set 1 ... }` then `if (*(char*)(param_1+0x3c4) == 1) { ... }`; Field_Object2D_BeginTouchEvent resets it to 0.

fields.name: timer
fields.evidence: `*(float*)(param_1+0x3c8) = *(float*)(param_1+0x3c8) + in_s0` accumulates the frame delta; compared against 0x3F7FFFFF (1.0f) and DAT_0060ec38 (0x3ECCCCCD, 0.4f) and reset to DAT_0060ec34 (0.0f); Field_Object2D_BeginTouchEvent resets it to 0.

summary: Streaming-audio transfer worker: owns the transfer thread handle, the transfer mutex at +8 and the stop/active flags; Sound_StreamThread_Main is the thread body and maybe_Sound_StreamThread_Destroy stops the transfer, joins the thread and closes the handle.
evidence: Sound_StreamThread_Main (0x005476B0) loops while *(u8*)(self+0x14)==0, locking/unlocking the mutex at self+8 with Os_LockMonitor (0x00117E50) / 0x00117ED0 and sleeping via 0x00114FAC. maybe_Sound_StreamThread_Destroy (0x005478F4) calls Snd_StopStreamTransfer (0x00547884) when +0x15 is set, then Thread::Join (0x00118170) and svcCloseHandle (svc 0x23) on *self. Snd_StopStreamTransfer's own doc confirms +0x14 = 'stopping' and +0x15 = 'transfer active'.

fields.name: threadHandle
fields.evidence: `if (*param_1 != 0) { software_interrupt(0x23); *param_1 = 0; }` in maybe_Sound_StreamThread_Destroy - svc 0x23 is svcCloseHandle, and Snd_StopStreamTransfer (0x00547884) closes the same word.

fields.name: stopRequested
fields.evidence: The main loop returns as soon as *(char*)(self+0x14) != 0 and re-tests it after every work step; Snd_StopStreamTransfer sets it to 1 to ask the worker to exit.

fields.name: isTransferActive
fields.evidence: maybe_Sound_StreamThread_Destroy calls Snd_StopStreamTransfer only `if (*(char*)((int)param_1 + 0x15) != 0)`; Snd_StopStreamTransfer clears it to 0 after closing the transfer handle.

summary: Wave-archive cache/loader: holds the sound-archive pointer, streams wave blocks through the archive's lock at +0x110 and can be aborted through a flag near the end of the object; the same 524-byte layout is also recorded as Sound_WaveArchive.
evidence: maybe_Sound_WaveCache_LoadDecoded (0x00549FFC) / LoadDecodedWithHeader (0x0054A230) / ReadBlocks (0x0054B12C) all start with FUN_00660b94(param_1[1]) and dispatch the vtable slot at *param_1+0x10; ReadBlocks unlocks *(int*)(param_1+4)+0x110 (Os_LockMonitor/0x00117ED0) and bails out when *(char*)(param_1+0x20a) is set. structs.json lists Sound_WaveArchive with the identical size 524 and the same offsets 4/64/522, so the two names describe one object.

fields.name: archive
fields.evidence: param_1[1] is passed to FUN_00660b94 (archive id), FUN_0065E340 (Sound_SeqParam_GetWaveRef) and FUN_0065E398; ReadBlocks locks/unlocks *(int*)(param_1+4)+0x110, i.e. the archive's monitor.

fields.name: unknown_vtableSlotPhantom
fields.evidence: PHANTOM: the only evidence is `(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x10))(param_1,uVar1)` - a vtable dispatch through slot 0x10, which struct_db mis-read as the array element param_1[0x10] = offset 0x40. No function reads or writes offset 64 directly; the real field is the vtable pointer at offset 0.

fields.name: maybe_abortRequested
fields.evidence: ReadBlocks (0x0054B12C) tests `if (*(char *)(param_1 + 0x20a) != '\0')` inside the transfer loop and jumps to the unlock/cleanup path; Sound_WaveArchive's twin reads the same byte as a cancel flag before its switch.

summary: Sound bank (CBNK) handle: Sound_Bank_ValidateHeader checks the 0x43424E4B magic and the 0x01000000..0x01000100 version, then stores the raw bank blob and the parsed bank table; Sound_Bank_BindWaveArchive reuses the same two words as {waveArchiveId, bankHandle}.
evidence: Sound_Bank_ValidateHeader (0x005493C0) zeroes +0/+4/+8, compares *param_2 with the literal 0x43424E4B at 0x00549420 and param_2[2]-0x01000000 < 0x101, then stores param_2 at +0, FUN_00662de0()+8 at +4 and 1 at +8. Sound_Bank_BindWaveArchive (0x0054C498) writes 0xFFFFFFFF/0 to the same two words and later stores the wave-archive id and the bank handle there, so the two functions use different objects with the same first two words.

fields.name: bankData
fields.evidence: Sound_Bank_ValidateHeader stores the validated raw bank pointer here (`*param_1 = (int)param_2`) after the 0x43424E4B magic and version check; Sound_Bank_BindWaveArchive instead stores the resolved wave-archive id.

fields.name: maybe_bankTable
fields.evidence: Sound_Bank_ValidateHeader stores FUN_00662de0()+8 here (`param_1[1] = iVar1 + 8`), the parsed bank table; Sound_Bank_BindWaveArchive stores the bank handle returned by FUN_00660330 in the same word.

summary: DSP audio-channel register interface: a double-buffered table of per-channel register blocks at +0x10B4 (two 0x60-byte banks) plus the two bank indices that select which bank the CPU writes and which one the DSP is playing.
evidence: Every method (Start 0x00518D04, Stop 0x00518D78, Pause 0x00518EA8, Flush 0x0051914C, SetLoopCount 0x00518DE8, SetWaveBuffer 0x00518F10, SetupSample 0x0051927C) resolves its channel block as *(u32**)(self + (*(u16*)(self+0x131E) & 1)*0x60 + ch*4 + 0x10B4) and then sets a bit in the block's first word (0x10000 start, 0x10 pause, 0x20000000 flush, 0x80000 wave, 0x40200000 sample). GetPlayPosition (0x00518E58) and UpdateSampleInfo (0x0051908C) index the status/info banks at +0x10AC and +0x1174 with the u16 at +0x1320. The generated type name Sound_DspChannel is kept verbatim (not SoundDspChannel) because structs.json and other batches already reference it in signatures.

fields.name: registerBankIndex
fields.evidence: `(*(ushort *)(param_1 + 0x131e) & 1) * 0x60` selects one of the two 0x60-byte banks of channel register-block pointers at +0x10B4 in Start/Stop/Pause/Flush/SetLoopCount/SetWaveBuffer/SetupSample/UpdateSampleInfo.

fields.name: statusBankIndex
fields.evidence: `*(ushort *)(param_1 + 0x1320)` indexes the channel status bank at +0x10AC in Sound_DspChannel_GetPlayPosition (0x00518E58, literal 0x00001320 at 0x00518EA4) and the channel info bank at +0x1174 in maybe_Sound_DspChannel_UpdateSampleInfo (0x0051908C).

summary: Polymorphic sequence-parameter facade: forwards each query to the base sequence-data object at +4 and ORs in the result of the same query on the optional extension object at +8, so a game-specific sequence can override the archive defaults.
evidence: All ten maybe_Sound_SeqParam_Get* methods have the identical shape `uVar1 = FUN_0066xxxx(*(u32*)(param_1+4)); piVar2 = *(int**)(param_1+8); if (piVar2 && (char)piVar2[1]) uVar3 = (**(code**)(*piVar2 + SLOT))(piVar2,...); return uVar1 | uVar3;` with slots 0x0C/0x18/0x1C/0x24/0x28/0x2C/0x38/0x3C/0x40/0x44/0x48/0x50. maybe_Sound_SeqParam_NotifyChange (0x00660330) dispatches on the top byte of the id (1 voice params, 3 header word, 5 wave ref, 6 range pair) and then calls vtable slot 0x10 on itself, so the object is polymorphic with the vtable at offset 0.

fields.name: baseSeqData
fields.evidence: *(u32*)(param_1+4) is the first argument of every base accessor: Sound_Seq_GetVoiceParamsBase (0x00660C30), Sound_Seq_GetTrackKindBase (0x006612B4), Sound_SeqTrack_ReadDescriptorA/B (0x00660E20/0x006610EC), 0x00660AF8, 0x00660BA4, 0x00660CF0, 0x00660D3C, 0x00660D5C, 0x00660DC8, 0x00660A94 and 0x006610B0.

fields.name: unknown_vtableSlotPhantom
fields.evidence: PHANTOM: the only evidence is `uVar3 = (**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x10))(param_1);` in maybe_Sound_SeqParam_NotifyChange (0x00660330) - a vtable dispatch through slot 0x10 that struct_db mis-read as param_1[0x10] = offset 0x40. No function reads or writes offset 64; the real field is the vtable pointer at offset 0.

summary: Streaming audio channel: a vtable/owner word, a buffer index and four 0x10-byte stream buffers constructed in place at +8; the recorded size of 8 only covers the two scalar words.
evidence: Sound_StreamChannel_InitBuffers (0x00541EC0) does `*self = vtable; self[1] = 0; std_ConstructArray(self + 2, _FUN_00541F10, 0x10, 4);` - std_ConstructArray (0x00100050) builds four 0x10-byte elements at +8, so the real object is at least 0x48 bytes even though the batch size is 8 (max_strong_field+width).

fields.name: maybe_vtable
fields.evidence: `*param_1 = param_2` where the readable doc names the second argument 'vtable'; nothing in the recovered code dispatches through it, so it could equally be an owner pointer (compare Sound_StreamGroup_Init, which stores its owner at +4).

fields.name: maybe_activeBufferIndex
fields.evidence: `param_1[1] = 0;` in Sound_StreamChannel_InitBuffers - cleared at construction and never read in the recovered code; the four 0x10-byte buffers it indexes follow at +8.

summary: Voice-slot group of a stream: stores the owner id at +4, four 0x10-byte voice-stealing slots at +8..+0x47 and an initialised guard; Sound_Stream_SetSource calls the one-time init when a stream first receives a source.
evidence: maybe_Sound_StreamGroup_Init (0x00541DA4) returns immediately when *(char*)(param_1+0x58) != 0, stores param_2 at +4, then calls Sound_Voice_SelectLowestPriority (0x0054B48C) on the four 0x10-byte slots at +8/+0x18/+0x28/+0x38 with thresholds 0x7FFFFFFF, 1, 1, 1, and finally sets +0x58 = 1 and +0x59 = 0. Its only caller is Sound_Stream_SetSource (0x0054260C).

fields.evidence: `if (*(char *)(param_1 + 0x58) != '\0') return;` guards the whole init and `*(undefined1 *)(param_1 + 0x58) = 1;` sets it at the end.

fields.name: maybe_flag59
fields.evidence: `*(undefined1 *)(param_1 + 0x59) = 0;` is the last statement of maybe_Sound_StreamGroup_Init; the byte is never read in the recovered methods, so its purpose is unknown.

summary: Grouping of the streaming-sound worker threads; the only recovered method is Gfx_ShutdownRenderServices (0x00383EC8), which shuts down the render services of the owning subsystem, so the Sound attribution of this class is doubtful.
evidence: maybe_Sound_StreamThreads_Shutdown (0x00383EC8) is named Gfx_ShutdownRenderServices in decomp/readable and its body contains no sound call at all: it signals/closes the two Gfx command buffers at 0x007CF2B8/0x007CF2E8, clears the four Gfx layer states (0x001F33E0/0x001F34C8/0x001F336C/0x001F3454), releases the object at +0x78 and stops the icon-cache service (0x0050A09C). Its 12 callers are Ui/Gfx code (Ui_GlobalObjects_Shutdown, Ui_Subsystem_Init, Ui_System_Update, Ui_GetRootSingleton).

fields.evidence: `if ((*(byte *)(param_1 + 0x68) & 1) != 0) { ... }` gates the whole shutdown and `*(uint *)(param_1 + 0x68) = *(uint *)(param_1 + 0x68) & 0xfffffffc;` clears bits 0 and 1 at the end, so it is a 32-bit flag word, not a byte.

fields.name: maybe_ownedService
fields.evidence: `if (*(int **)(param_1 + 0x78) != (int *)0x0) { (**(code **)(**(int **)(param_1 + 0x78) + 4))(); *(undefined4 *)(param_1 + 0x78) = 0; }` - a polymorphic object released through vtable slot 1 (deleting destructor) and then nulled.

summary: Background-music channel manager: maybe_Sound_BgmChannel_Create builds a sequence player from the sound-system handle at +0x8C and the other methods load, restore and command it; the single field recorded in this batch is a mis-attributed stack local.
evidence: maybe_Sound_BgmChannel_Create (0x00163254) reads *(u32*)(param_1+0x8C) as the sound-system handle, allocates through FUN_005ffd40 and initialises the new player's +0x48/+0x49/+0x54/+0x58/+0x5C/+0x60/+0x1E8. maybe_Sound_BgmChannel_Command (0x001634CC) is damaged decompilation (unaff_rN, in_crN, halt_baddata) and must stay maybe_ with confidence <= 0.3.

summary: Resolved sound-resource handle: a pointer to the raw resource blob plus a loaded flag; Sound_Resource_CheckMagic returns 1 only when the flag is set and the blob's header word matches the expected magic.
evidence: Sound_Resource_CheckMagic (0x006609FC) is `if (((char)param_1[3] == '\0') || (iVar3 = *param_1, iVar1 = FUN_0065f420(iVar3), *(int *)(iVar3 + iVar1) != DAT_00660a34)) return 0; else return 1;` - FUN_0065f420 returns the blob's data-section offset and DAT_00660a34 is the expected magic. The same 16-byte layout is used by Sound_WaveInfo (offsets 0/4/8/0xC).

fields.evidence: `if (((char)param_1[3] == '\0') || ...) { uVar2 = 0; }` - the magic check is skipped and 0 returned while this byte is zero; maybe_Sound_WaveInfo_ParseFormat and maybe_Sound_WaveInfo_GetChannelDataOffset use the same byte as the 'resolved' guard.

summary: Sequence-data object as seen by the track reader: the two ReadDescriptor methods resolve a record from the sequence blob at +0x3C and unpack the four 0xD-byte track descriptors, branching on the sequence version at +8.
evidence: Sound_SeqTrack_ReadDescriptorA (0x00660E20) and ReadDescriptorB (0x006610EC) both start with FUN_0065f678(*(u32*)(param_1+0x3c)) and then compare *(u32*)(param_1+8) against DAT_006610a0/a4/ac / DAT_006611a4 to pick the old or new record layout; ReadDescriptorA fills four 0xD-byte track entries at param_3+4.

fields.evidence: `iVar4 = FUN_0065f678(*(undefined4 *)(param_1 + 0x3c));` in both ReadDescriptorA and ReadDescriptorB - the pointer to the sequence blob whose record table is resolved by 24-bit id (FUN_0065f678 reads [blob+4] as a table offset and indexes 8-byte entries).
